claims.text: The studied material is a CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy multilayer coating.
Adjusting sputter power and substrate temperature can produce CoCrFeMnNi coatings spanning highly coherent to semi-coherent interfaces.
The degree of interface coherency governs whether dislocations are transmitted or blocked.
Highly coherent multilayer interfaces are strong barriers to dislocation motion.
Highly coherent interfaces cause dislocation pileup.
Highly coherent interfaces cause strain partitioning across layers.
Dislocation blockage, pileup, and interlayer strain partitioning retard the accumulation of time-dependent plastic deformation.
Coatings with highly coherent interfaces will have significantly lower creep rates than coatings with semi-coherent interfaces.
Coatings with highly coherent interfaces will accumulate less total creep strain than coatings with semi-coherent interfaces.
Cross-sectional TEM will reveal fewer detectable dislocation networks in highly coherent-interface coatings than in semi-coherent-interface coatings.
Semi-coherent-interface coatings will exhibit higher creep rates under otherwise identical test conditions.
Semi-coherent-interface coatings will exhibit more extensive dislocation activity under otherwise identical test conditions.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply to CoCrFeMnNi multilayer coatings tested by nanoindentation creep at 300–500 °C.
Application outside 300–500 °C or to substantially different alloy systems requires additional validation.
A valid comparison requires microstructural homogeneity apart from interface coherency.
Deposition-induced microstructural variations may confound isolation of the effect of interface coherency.
Failure of the highly coherent-interface coatings to show a significantly lower creep rate than the semi-coherent-interface coatings would falsify the proposed governing role of interface coherency.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts that highly coherent interfaces produce dislocation pileup, whereas the falsification rule treats reduced dislocation pileup in the highly coherent coatings as the expected result. The direction of the pileup prediction is therefore internally inconsistent.
